title: Tidy src/FsAnalyser.Core: HF-001, HF-003, HF-005, HF-006, HF-011, HF-024
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: HF-024's 'better' fix is not built, as in attempt 1: both figures from one quota-independent source (GetDiskSpaceInformationW or FileFsFullSizeInformation). The guard now refuses both wrap-around bounds, but a quota above the volume's free space still gives a positive, mixed figure.
HF-005: links were removed from ScanProgress rather than shown in the counters line, as in attempt 1.

HF-024 residual, as in attempt 1: a per-user quota above the volume's free space still gives a positive but mixed used figure (quota total less volume free). A quota-independent source (GetDiskSpaceInformationW's Actual* allocation units, or FileFsFullSizeInformation) would fix it, after re-measuring against Get-Volume.

The SL-039 App store rule (`(?<!\bresult)\.Store\b`) has no xUnit twin, so `dotnet test` stays green when it breaks, which is how attempt 1 missed it. It also forbids App files outside FolderTree*.cs from naming the EntryKind enum, not only from reading a store. A person may want to decide whether an enum import should be allowed, or whether the rule should get a twin in ArchitectureRulesTests.
HF-001: MainWindow's note still says 'This drive does not report file IDs', though with the value-based flag it can also show when only some files lacked an ID.

not reached: A real volume that answers the extended directory class but lists files with no ID or a sentinel ID (HF-001's triggering case). No such volume is reachable. The FAT32 EFI partition has no letter and mounting it needs an administrator, and this stage does not create SMB mappings for the loopback rig. That case is proven only through the ScanOptions.ListedFileId seam.

not reached: A per-user NTFS quota smaller than the volume's free space (HF-024's triggering case). Enabling quotas needs an administrator and is not a named elevated operation. A session would be needed, but the arithmetic is fully covered by the pure TryUsedBytes test, so a session looks unnecessary.

not reached: The HF-024 residual left open by build: a quota above the volume's free space still gives a positive figure that mixes the quota total with the volume's free space. Nothing was checked for this case.

not reached: Whether MainWindow's note wording ('This drive does not report file IDs') reads correctly when only some files lacked an ID. This is left open by build, and no real volume produced the note.
